text: A worker should not repeat a known mistake just because its conversation disappeared. THE SPINE makes its memory change the decision.

This is a controlled crisis fixture. Session A writes a structured lesson into real Sibyl memory and exits. This new process has no chat history. It reads the same store and reduces equity. Now remove only the memory. Same frame, another fresh process: no lesson, and the policy returns to fifty-five percent equity. The database changed; the input did not.

Recall is not the only defense. A stored hard lesson can block a risky proposal even when text retrieval misses. This receipt shows the proposal, the guard's verdict, and the replacement that reaches the action adapter. It is a dry run; no transaction is claimed.
The store also exposes what it does not know. Missing evidence becomes a learning task. Coverage changes only after a lesson is acquired, not because the agent claimed it learned.
Across two hundred seeded frames, memory changes seventy-five percent of decisions and averts seven point zero seven two percentage points of simulated mean loss. The model and reproducer are public.

A historical Base transaction anchors a memory root. The action adapter uses symbolic transfers, not portfolio trades. A separate x402 endpoint sells static snapshot metadata. Our two settlement tests were self-funded; we are not presenting them as customer demand.

The buyer is an operator whose workers must preserve constraints across restarts. The next milestone is a measured external pilot. THE SPINE: persisted experience, guarded decisions, and evidence you can inspect.
